source.title: Behavioral Convergence Without Representational Convergence: Persistent Training-History Dependence in Neural Networks

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether similar behavior after common training entails representational convergence, and finds persistent representation differences tied to prior training history. It refines the scope of convergence claims rather than testing convergence across model scale or architecture.
record.gate_note: The paper directly measures representation similarity with a CKA-derived history score. Accuracy and prediction-disagreement results are included as context for the representation measurements. Fresh linear-probe results do not map one model's representations onto another's, so they are not rows for V4. The paper does not compare alternative representation-similarity metrics.
record.test_reason: The study measures CKA similarity between paired same-architecture CNNs that differ only in early task order and then share long common training. Their alignment stays incomplete (mean CKA about 0.81–0.87) and does not decay toward full agreement through 50,000 updates. This bears on V7's claim that alignment stays incomplete and may plateau, in a small controlled setting. It does not test scale, modality, different initializations, mapping or metric dependence.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that similar final behaviour need not imply similar internal representations, and that training history stays measurable after long common training. They scope this to MNIST, a compact CNN, CKA at two layers and a finite 50k-update horizon, and claim neither permanence nor a universal mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a controlled sequential task-order reversal followed by common relaxation, measuring a CKA-derived history score in a compact CNN. It does not reproduce a cross-model scale-alignment method.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured residue is lower under LeakyReLU than ReLU at 25,000 and 50,000 updates in the matched-rate control; the study does not compare similarity metrics or probe settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Frozen FC1 linear probes recover practically equivalent class accuracy from both histories at 500 examples per class (diff +0.090 pp, TOST equivalence). Small advantages appear for the A-first (SABC) history at low data budgets (+0.58 pp at 50 per class, p=0.027).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representations that differ in CKA geometry can carry equivalent linearly decodable task information.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing ReLU with LeakyReLU at matched learning rate reduces the 50k-update history residue by 0.040 in all five paired seeds (p=0.097 t-test). Prediction disagreement falls from 2.56% to 1.44%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual representational divergence after common training depends on activation-mediated plasticity.

record.problems: All experiments use MNIST and a compact CNN; the primary representation result uses linear CKA at Conv2 and FC1 only. Long-horizon, rotated-MNIST, and activation controls each use five paired seeds. The LeakyReLU learning rate was selected after numerical instability at the initial rate, and persistence is shown only through a finite 50,000-update horizon.
record.rows_left_out: Fresh linear-probe accuracy results assess class information accessible to separate readouts, not representation alignment or a map between the paired representations. Accuracy gaps and prediction disagreements are behavioral diagnostics rather than representation-similarity outcomes.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep, and no models differing in architecture, objective or data source.
No vision–language or paired image–caption models.
Pairs share an identical initialization, so there is no test of convergence across different initializations.
No cross-model linear map, stitching, relative representations or unpaired alignment. The linear probes are separate readouts, not maps between the models.
No neuron-, SAE-feature- or circuit-level recurrence analysis.
Only linear CKA at Conv2/FC1 on one in-distribution probe set. Metric, settings and input dependence are not varied.

Does not test whether shared data or objectives, rather than a common model of reality, explain cross-model alignment. Does not compare independently trained models of different architectures or data. Only a compact MNIST CNN is studied.

missing.what: Trajectory of Hrepr over common-relaxation checkpoints 0–10,000 in the 20-seed experiment. The figure shows accuracy gaps contracting while Hrepr stays above zero, which bears on plateau; no per-checkpoint numbers are given in the text.

record.verdict_notes: This is a path-dependence study, not a cross-model convergence study. Its link to the phenomenon is mainly that representational alignment between models trained on the same final data stays incomplete and does not decay. The single metric (linear CKA), the tiny model and the five-seed controls limit how far it generalises. The reader's limits_scope label for r8–r10 was dropped: the activation contrast changes the size of the residue, not whether alignment stays incomplete.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability scaling sweep, or comparison across independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data.
The paired networks share initialization and differ in task order; the study does not test different initializations for shared features or subspaces.
No cross-model mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment test.
No recurrence of interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits is tested.

No comparison across similarity metrics, metric settings, or out-of-distribution probes. The rotated-MNIST control tests whether the result persists in a changed training protocol, not whether measured convergence depends on probe inputs.

The study tests residual representation differences after common relaxation in a compact MNIST CNN. It does not compare different architectures, modalities, objectives, or data sources, or establish that shared data/objectives rather than a common model of reality explain cross-model alignment.

relationships.condition: Compact MNIST CNN pairs with the same initialization and reversed task order, followed by identical common training (class-split and same-label rotated-MNIST protocols, ReLU and LeakyReLU at matched learning rate)
relationships.reason: Representations never fully align despite near-identical accuracy. Hrepr is 0.139–0.165 at matched or 10k endpoints (r1, r2, r6, r7). It does not decay over 10k→50k updates (r3–r5: 0.153→0.190). It persists under both activations (r8–r10). The residual gap is moderate (CKA ≈0.81–0.87) rather than large.
relationships.display_finding: Despite near-identical accuracy, Hrepr remained 0.139–0.165 at matched or 10,000-update endpoints, with moderate residual differences reflected in CKA of approximately 0.81–0.87; the gap persisted under ReLU and LeakyReLU and did not decay from 10,000 to 50,000 updates, with Hrepr changing from 0.153 to 0.190.

relation.reason: The study directly measures representational similarity after reversed training histories and identical common training.

tranche.reason: Controlled common-training experiments show incomplete representational convergence despite similar accuracy, qualifying convergence claims over the measured finite horizon.

source_check.notes: Evidence is restricted to a compact MNIST CNN, linear CKA at Conv2/FC1, and finite training horizons. Paired models share initialization; similar accuracy does not imply identical predictions or interchangeable representations.
